author: human
request:
Bug report: opening /owners?page=0 — or any page value below 1 — renders the
error page instead of the owner list. Expected behavior: the owner listing
treats any page value below 1 as the first page and responds with the normal
listing (HTTP 200). Find the cause, fix it, and cover the fix with a test.

author: product-requirements-expert
title: Owner list treats a page number below 1 as the first page
summary: Opening the owner list with a page number of 0 or below currently shows the error page. The owner list must instead treat any page number below 1 as the first page and respond with the normal listing (HTTP 200).
acceptance_criteria: given a page number of 0 or below, when the owner list is opened, then the first page of owners is listed normally with HTTP 200 and no error page is shown
given a last name matching more than one owner and a page number below 1, when the search runs, then the first page of matches is listed
given a page number far below 1, such as a large negative number, when the owner list is opened, then the first page is listed, the same as for 0 (Owner records edge case 4)
the listing served for a page number below 1 presents itself as the first page, the same as a request for page 1
non_goals: Page numbers above the last page are not in this slice; the owner did not raise them
Non-numeric page values are not in this slice; the request covers page values below 1 only
Paging in the veterinarian directory is not in this slice; the request names the owner list only
notes: Owner request (intake line 1): treat any page value below 1 as the first page, respond with the normal listing (HTTP 200), find the cause, fix it, cover it with a test. The intake records no decisions; this dispatch made two reversible calls. (1) The rule covers every owner listing, with or without a last-name search, because both are the same paged listing. (2) The listing presents itself as page 1, because the owner asked that the value be treated as the first page. Observed cause, for the design expert only: the 1-based page number becomes a 0-based page request, which rejects negative indexes, so page 0 and below fail. docs/architecture-principles.md records request-parameter normalization to a permitted range as binding at the web boundary. The single test name is data-driven over page values (0, -1, a large negative) and over the no-search and multi-match cases. The PRD edit adds REQ-OWN-005 to the Owner records narrative, two Done-when bullets, and edge case 4. No Non-Goals row changed.

author: system-design-expert
architectural_fit: Covered by the existing OwnerController contract (system-design.md § Contracts, now also implementing REQ-OWN-005) and the Web controller row of architecture-principles.md § pattern catalog, which classes normalizing a request parameter to its permitted range as binding rather than a business rule. No new type, module, or pattern is involved. The owner listing handler (GET /owners, processFindForm) clamps the 1-based page parameter to at least 1 before it is used, and it uses the clamped value both to build the page request and as the currentPage model attribute. The fix lives in the controller, not the repository. Basis: grep of OwnerController.java (lines 95, 121, 126, 135), not an IDE-oracle resolution; the IDE oracle is not connected. Root cause confirmed: PageRequest.of(page - 1, pageSize) rejects a negative index, so page 0 and below reach the error page.
integration_points: Boundary: OwnerRepository, the persistence boundary. Double: the existing class-level @MockitoBean OwnerRepository in OwnerControllerTests, a framework stub kept as a conscious exception (testing-principles.md § Mocking Policy). A hand-written double does not fit because OwnerRepository extends JpaRepository, so a double would have to implement every inherited method, and the new test joins a @WebMvcTest fixture that already supplies the stub. Stub findByLastNameStartingWith with any Pageable. Assert that the Pageable passed has page number 0, and that the model's currentPage is 1.
Boundary: HTTP transport. Double: MockMvc under @WebMvcTest(OwnerController.class), the sanctioned web test harness (testing-principles.md § Mocking Policy).

Binding: no new entry point. The existing GET /owners handler keeps its scalar int page request parameter as the binding target; the slice only normalizes its range (architecture-principles.md Web controller row).

patterns.description: processFindForm: normalize page once at entry and pass the normalized value to both findPaginatedForOwnersLastName and addPaginationModel

existing multi-owner listing test shape (PageImpl of two owners, view owners/ownersList) to copy for the data-driven test over page values 0, -1, and a large negative, with and without a lastName search (testing-principles.md parameterized-test row)

risks.risk: Normalizing only the value passed to the query leaves currentPage at the raw value, so the listing would not present itself as page 1 (acceptance criterion 4)
risks.mitigation: Apply one clamp at handler entry and reuse the clamped value for both the query and the model (architecture-principles.md Web controller row: normalization is binding at the boundary)

risks.risk: Integer.MIN_VALUE - 1 overflows to Integer.MAX_VALUE, so clamping after the subtraction, or computing page - 1 before the clamp, would silently yield an empty page instead of the first page
risks.mitigation: Clamp the 1-based value first (for example with Math.max(page, 1)) and subtract afterwards. Include Integer.MIN_VALUE, or another large negative, among the test's data rows (PRD Owner records edge case 4)

risks.risk: The owner listing path scales with the number of owners, but system-design.md has no § Scale and Load section to cite
risks.mitigation: Simplest readable form. The slice adds constant work to a listing already bounded by the fixed page size recorded under system-design.md § Constants, and it changes no query or data-scaling behavior

notes: Autofix audit: no design-doc-autofix records in the log, skipped. Durable-memory gap: system-design.md has no § Scale and Load section. This slice adds no path that scales with data, so the section is left for a slice that does. Sibling defect observed, out of scope under this slice's non-goals: VetController.findPaginated uses the same PageRequest.of(page - 1, ...) form, so /vets.html?page=0 fails the same way. It is surfaced for the product expert to raise as its own slice. It is not recorded in Known Defects here because this triage has no product basis for it. The single-match redirect branch and the not-found branch are unaffected by the clamp.

author: test-reviewer
recommendations: Optional: NEGATIVE_PAGE (-1) and PAGE_ZERO fall in the same equivalence class (page < 1), and the with/without-search variants take the same clamp path. Only 0, which is the boundary, and Integer.MIN_VALUE, which covers the overflow, are distinct. Dropping -1 would remove two cases that a plausible change would not fail.

Optional: the captor plus getPageNumber() picks a field instead of comparing a whole Pageable. Comparing against PageRequest.of(FIRST_PAGE_INDEX, <size>) would need the production page size, which is hidden coupling. The captor is a defensible choice here, and no finding is raised.
approved_aspects: ./gradlew test --tests '*OwnerControllerTests' passed (BUILD SUCCESSFUL, jacocoTestReport ran). Without the clamp, page 0 would build PageRequest.of(-1) and fail, so the test would catch a regression.
Placement: system-design.md assigns request handling to OwnerController, so a MockMvc web-layer test is the right level. No production helper was widened.

coverage-map REQ-OWN-005 lists 2 Done-when bullets and edge case 4 (far-negative page). The one declared test, theOwnerListShouldShowTheFirstPageWhenThePageNumberIsBelowOne, is present. Its cases cover 0, -1 and Integer.MIN_VALUE, each with and without a lastName search that matches two owners.

Name follows the the{Subject}Should{Outcome} school. Data is named by role (PAGE_ZERO, FAR_NEGATIVE_PAGE, SOME_LAST_NAME_PREFIX). Owner construction sits behind createAnOwner(). The test body is straight-line with four phases, and AssertJ is used for the captor value.

author: change-grader
summary: clamp owner-list page number below 1 to the first page

blast_radius.note: One production method (OwnerController.processFindForm) gains a single Math.max clamp and two argument swaps; the rest is one test file and two doc lines, all in one module, nothing sensitive. The extractor's 16 hunks is a zero-context count; the unified diff has 12, and the gap is only import and anchor lines splitting.

semantic_surprise.note: Reading the hunks: the clamp runs before the existing page - 1 conversion, so Integer.MIN_VALUE cannot overflow. The clamped value feeds both the query and the currentPage model attribute, with no operator or boundary inversion. Pages of 1 and above pass through unchanged, and the single-match redirect and not-found branches keep their existing logic.

test_adequacy.note: The parameterized MockMvc test covers 0, -1 and Integer.MIN_VALUE, with and without a multi-match search. It asserts HTTP 200, the list view, currentPage 1, and a captured Pageable index of 0. Without the fix, page 0 would throw from PageRequest.of(-1), and the MIN_VALUE row would capture index MAX_VALUE, so the test fails against a broken implementation.

reviewer_hedging.note: All three rostered reviewers approved in the first round with no findings; security was scoped out by the plan, so its silence is expected. The test-reviewer's two recommendations are marked optional polish about redundant -1 rows and the captor style, not correctness worries. The spot-checked citations resolve (architecture-principles.md:85, system-design.md:72).

scope_deviation.note: No design revisions, consultations or build retries. The diff touches only the owner listing named by the requirement. The identical PageRequest.of(page - 1) in VetController.java:61 is left alone, as the non-goals require; the design expert surfaced it as a candidate follow-up slice.

rationale: A small, well-placed fix. The clamp precedes the 0-based conversion, covers the overflow case, and feeds both the query and the displayed page. The tests would fail without it and the reviewers approved cleanly. A glance confirms it. Separately, consider a follow-up slice for the same defect in VetController.
